title: Senior Product Manager - Measurement & Reporting
description:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.

About the Role 

You’ll own Measurement & Reporting: the product surface where Vibe turns campaign delivery into proof. Performance is why clients pick Vibe. Trusted, actionable measurement is why they stay and scale with us.

Reporting to the VP of Product, you’ll own the strategy and roadmap for how Vibe explains and proves the impact of CTV advertising across every vertical. Your main focus will be ecom and CPG, with growing coverage of apps, local, and travel. The goal is to make CTV outcomes as trustworthy and actionable as search and social, so clients confidently move more budget to Vibe.

You’ll work daily with Data Science, Data Platform, Engineering, and our client-facing teams (CS, Sales, TAM). With Walmart’s purchase data now part of the platform, measurement is becoming one of Vibe’s biggest differentiators.

What You’ll Do 

Reporting & Insight 

- Own advertiser-facing reporting, including dashboards, outcome metrics, and exports that make CTV performance clear to both technical and non-technical buyers.

- Turn raw performance data into benchmarks and insights clients can grasp at a glance.

Attribution & Incrementality 

- Productize attribution and incrementality to a client-grade standard, not just an internal signal.

- Own integrations with the measurement tools clients already trust, such as MMPs, web/CAPI pixels, MMM, and third-party partners (e.g. Northbeam, Haus), so Vibe’s numbers hold up next to Meta and Google.

- Guarantee data accuracy, transparent methodology, and defensible results.

Activation 

- Translate measurement into clear recommendations and next actions that drive spend decisions.

- Close the loop between proven outcomes and campaign optimization, powering the “more performance → more spend” flywheel.

- Partner with CS, Sales, and TAM to make measurement the core of how we retain and grow clients.

- Use SQL and log-level data to validate methodologies, size opportunities, and prioritize by impact.

What You Need 

- 5+ years in Product Management on performance AdTech, measurement/attribution, or analytics products.

- Strong grasp of digital measurement (attribution models, incrementality and causal testing, MMM) and of why click-based models break for CTV.

- Solid statistical literacy, including experimental design, holdouts, significance, and confidence intervals.

- A track record of shipping client-facing reporting or insight products, and of making complex data simple and trustworthy for marketers.

- Fluency with outcome KPIs across verticals and with the ecom/CPG performance stack.

- Hands-on SQL and data exploration, and you’re comfortable in technical, data-intensive environments.

- The ability to bridge technical measurement and business/GTM stakeholders.

Why This Role 

- You’ll own the product domain that decides whether clients trust their Vibe spend, and whether they scale it.

- You’ll have a direct line to revenue, because measurement is Vibe’s main lever for retaining and growing clients.

- You’ll shape how an entire category proves CTV as a performance channel.

- You’ll have high autonomy and influence across functions, from data science to clients’ C-suite.

Our Values 

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

You’ll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.

This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you’ll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that’s moving fast.

description:
About Mirakl: 

Founded in 2012, Mirakl has been at the forefront of marketplace innovation, empowering every business to compete in the platform economy.

Today, Mirakl's operating system combines an enterprise marketplace solution (Mirakl Platform) that enables retailers and B2B organizations to launch, scale, and operate marketplaces and dropship, AI-powered multichannel selling (Mirakl Connect), retail media (Mirakl Ads) and an agentic commerce infrastructure (Mirakl Nexus).

With dual headquarters in Boston and Paris, Mirakl helps a global ecosystem of 450+ marketplaces (B2C and B2B) and a network of over 100k third-party marketplace sellers. Brands like Macy's, Decathlon, Carrefour, Asos, and Airbus Helicopters use Mirakl to grow their businesses in new and remarkable ways.

For more information, visit www.mirakl.com .

Mirakl in Numbers: 

- 🗓️ Founded in 2012 | Member of French Tech Next40

- 👥 750+ employees in 9 offices worldwide: Paris, Barcelona, Bordeaux, Boston, London, Munich, New York, Sydney, Tokyo

Our Values: 

Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.

Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:

- 💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success

- 🏆 Get Things Done: We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results

- 🚀 Go Above & Beyond: We tackle challenges proactively and always aim for excellence

- 🎓 Succeed Through Expertise: Knowledge sharing and continuous learning are core to our culture

- 🤝 Satisfy & Empower Clients: We're committed to our clients' success

About the role

Mirakl is looking for a senior contractor to join its Finance team and provide operational leadership in an international, multi-entity environment.

Reporting to the Accounting & Tax Director, you will secure the continuity and quality of day-to-day accounting operations while supporting the monthly and annual close.

The role also offers the opportunity to contribute to the transformation of the Finance function, particularly through the identification, testing and adoption of relevant automation and AI use cases. The successful candidate will combine strong accounting expertise with a pragmatic, hands-on approach to process improvement and change management.

Contractor 

6 months 

Start: ASAP 

Location: Paris or Bordeaux (aller-retour à prévoir à Bordeaux 1 fois par mois) 

Key responsibilities

Accounts Payable and Procure-to-Pay

- Own and coordinate the end-to-end Procure-to-Pay process, from supplier creation and invoice receipt through to validation, booking and payment.

- Coordinate the Accounts Payable team and ensure timely processing of invoices across Mirakl's entities.

- Monitor invoice workflows, approvals, purchase orders, blocked invoices and outstanding supplier balances.

- Review invoice coding, supporting documentation and accounting treatment, and act as an escalation point for complex supplier issues.

- Coordinate payment runs and ensure that payment files are prepared accurately and in line with internal approval procedures.

- Maintain robust controls over vendor master data, bank details, payment approvals and segregation of duties.

Accounting operations and close support

- Support the Accounting & Tax Director in the coordination of the monthly and annual close process.

- Review AP-related cut-off and other accounting entries.

- Monitor the reconciliation and clean-up of relevant balance sheet accounts and support the review of intercompany transactions.

- Coordinate with local accounting firms and external service providers across Mirakl's international perimeter.

- Contribute to audit preparation and respond to requests from external auditors and other stakeholders.

- Ensure that accounting evidence, procedures and control documentation are complete, accessible and up to date.

Finance transformation, automation and AI

- Contribute to Mirakl's Finance AI transformation roadmap by identifying high-value use cases within AP, Procure-to-Pay and accounting operations.

- Participate in discovery phases, workshops and experiments aimed at improving invoice processing, data quality, reconciliations, reporting and operational support.

- Help assess and test AI-enabled workflows, automation solutions and Finance agents, working closely with Finance, Data and other stakeholders.

- Translate operational requirements into clear process, data and control requirements for automation and AI initiatives.

- Support the adoption of new tools by documenting processes, defining operating guidelines, monitoring results and helping teams embed new ways of working.

- Remain attentive to data quality, confidentiality, traceability, human oversight and appropriate controls when using AI in Finance processes.

Candidate profile

- 8+ years of experience in accounting, finance operations or accounting management

- Previous experience as an Accounting Manager, Deputy Accounting Director

- Experience in a multi-entity, international environment; experience in a fast-growing technology or SaaS company is a strong advantage.

- Solid understanding of accounting principles, closing processes, cut-off, reconciliations and internal controls.

- Experience working with external accounting firms and international subsidiaries.

- Strong knowledge of ERP and finance systems

- Interest in Finance transformation, automation and AI, with the ability to translate operational needs into practical use cases.

- Autonomous, hands-on and solution-oriented, with excellent organisational, analytical and communication skills.

- Fluent English required; French is a strong advantage.

We welcome collaborators with their diverse perspectives and experiences to power us forward. These often far exceed conventional job requirements and help us create a culture of continuous learning. title: Solution Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
IDnow is a leader in digital identity and fraud prevention in Europe with a mission to transform trust into the most powerful asset in the digital world, empowering enterprises with AI-driven, SaaS-based identity solutions that deliver scalable security, adaptive compliance, and real-time fraud prevention . Through its broad portfolio of digital identity and fraud prevention solutions, IDnow establishes, maintains and enriches trust throughout the customer journey, ensuring businesses can confidently and securely operate while leveraging digital identity to drive growth, security and scalability. 

The company has offices in Germany, United Kingdom, Romania and France , and is backed by renowned institutional investors, including Corsair Capital and Seventure Partners. Its portfolio of international clients spans a wide range of end markets including financial services, telecommunications, travel & mobility, gaming, and other industries. 

This position is based in Rennes, France. 

The Solutions Engineer at IDnow is the client's trusted advisor through pre-sales and integration . You design the solution the client will rely on, you give them confidence that it will work in their environment, and you become the person they turn to for technical and solution decisions. Your focus is the technical side of the journey up to the point where the client is live on our products, and you make that path smooth . 

This is a hands-on, deeply technical role, and a commercial one . Solutions Engineers carry a quota and are measured on two things: the deals they help win, and whether the client goes live successfully. You work hand in hand with Sales to convince the client that our solution is the right one and to move them toward signature, and then you make sure they can use it well in production. You earn that through technical depth, but you are client-facing, credible and persuasive in a sales motion. You do this across our whole client base.

We hire this role at more than one level. The core of the job is the same; the scope you own and the complexity you handle grow with your experience. This role carries real ownership across the client journey, and a say in how the work evolves.

Key Responsibilities

Discover and Design

- Lead technical discovery, qualifying conversion rates, false acceptance and rejection trade-offs, fraud exposure and integration constraints before proposing a solution,

- Design end-to-end solution architectures that orchestrate document verification, digital identity, fraud signals, biometric authentication, eID and EU Digital Identity Wallet flows, and e-signature,

- Link every technical choice to the client’s business objectives and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), so proposals speak to outcomes rather than features,

- Define defensible architecture decisions covering fallback logic, data residency, scalability and performance,

- Support Sales with proposals, Requests for Proposal (RFPs) and Requests for Information (RFIs), advising on which capabilities to combine and why.

Prove, Integrate and Go Live

- Lead proof-of-concept and pilot engagements, configuring Application Programming Interface (API) integrations, building Postman collections and managing sandbox environments,

- Validate behaviour under realistic conditions and document what the client needs to go live,

- Guide client developers through API and mobile Software Development Kit (SDK) integration, including webhooks, authentication and testing,

- Troubleshoot integration issues by reading logs and diagnosing failures at the API and SDK level, rather than only forwarding them,

- Maintain a living integration map of the client’s architecture, data flows and dependencies,

- Own the account from signature to go-live, running the go-live plan and handing a documented account to Customer Success and Support at the end of hypercare.

Advise and Enable

- Build trusted advisor relationships with business and technical stakeholders, from first conversation to go-live,

- Represent the client’s technical reality internally, feeding integration blockers, product gaps and pilot learnings back to Product and Sales teams,

- Work with the internal escalation team on deeper platform issues, arriving with clear technical context,

- Stand alongside Sales in client meetings, addressing objections on integration effort, feasibility and alternatives,

- Improve demo environments, architecture templates and integration guides, and mentor team members as the practice grows.

Preferred Experience

You ask before you propose and qualify before you demo, turning ambiguous client requirements into the right technical solution. You take ownership of the client’s technical path from first conversation to production, and you explain complex systems in plain language to engineers and business leaders alike. You combine hands-on engineering depth with a commercial mindset, and you enjoy working alongside Sales to move a decision forward.

- Engineering or technical degree , a Master’s degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience,

- 3+ years of experience in solutions engineering, technical consulting, or implementation and onboarding in SaaS , ideally in identity, FinTech or security,

- Discovery and qualification skills , with the ability to turn an ambiguous client requirement into the best technical solution,

- Solution architecture skills , including designing integration flows, explaining orchestration logic and defending trade-offs with a client’s engineers,

title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (Inference Stack Optimization)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and we run the models underneath it ourselves.

Kimchi Inference 

One API line and a customer's existing client just works: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron served serverless from our own GPU fleet (OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible, pay per token, spend visible per user, team, and key). When control matters, the same models run on the customer's own cluster instead. Behind that one line sits the machinery you'll own: SGLang and vLLM engines, B300 nodes, a shared cluster filesystem that holds every checkpoint exactly once, KV caches riding coding traffic with heavy prefix reuse, and the benchmark harness that gates every change we ship.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. Cold starts. Cost per token.

Move those four numbers in the right direction and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every loader you tune, every scheduler decision you land, every kernel you stare at shows up in a customer's p99 and on our P&L. Your mandate is the inference stack's optimization, whatever it takes, and the technical direction of how we optimize it is yours to argue with data.

The problem: the checkpoints run 0.3-1.5 TB, and the "right" serving configuration depends on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, and quantization tolerance, all variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a configuration once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. We don't: we took Kimi-K3 (1.5 TB) from over an hour cold-to-serving to under twelve minutes with a shared filesystem, O_DIRECT weight loaders, and node-local JIT caches, and we're nowhere near done. Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV caches are next.

Stack: Python; SGLang; vLLM; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; fastsafetensors; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; virtiofs shared filesystems; ClickHouse; OpenTelemetry; Prometheus; Grafana; GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've built real ML systems for 5+ years, and your portfolio shows depth in inference or training infrastructure, not just model training notebooks.

- Your Python is production-grade: services, not scripts.

- You've run vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM for real, and you have a working mental model of why an engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- You've measured quantization regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node setups hold no fear: tensor and expert parallelism, collective communication, and their practical failure modes.

- You know where the bytes live (page caches, O_DIRECT, network filesystems under terabyte-scale reads) and how fast they move.

- You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell a real win from a benchmark artifact.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with draft models, CUDA-graph capture, and scheduler tuning across the engine
fleet. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and inter-token latency separately; profile to find the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, storage, or
network) and fix it, not the one you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Hierarchical and paged attention, prefix caching on heavy-reuse coding traffic, eviction policies, quantized KV. A lot of the
unrealized throughput lives here, and you'll own it.

- Kill cold starts. Weight loaders (O_DIRECT, fastsafetensors-class), JIT and compile caches, shared-filesystem read paths. A 1.5 TB checkpoint has no business
taking an hour to reach serving.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8/INT4, FP8/FP4 across weights, activations, and KV, measured on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, prefill/decode disaggregation, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck
on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible
experiments.

What’s in it for you?

- Competitive salary (depending on the level of experience).

- Enjoy a flexible, remote-first global environment.

- Collaborate with a global team of cloud experts and innovators, passionate about pushing the boundaries of Kubernetes technology

- Equity options.

- Get quick feedback with a fast-paced workflow. Most feature projects are completed in 1 to 4 weeks.

- Spend 10% of your work time on personal projects or self-improvement. 

- Learning budget for professional and personal development - including access to international conferences and courses that elevate your skills.

- Annual hackathon to spark new ideas and strengthen team bonds.

- Team-building budget and company events to connect with your colleagues.

- Equipment budget to ensure you have everything you need.

- Extra days off to help maintain a healthy work-life balance.

Hiring process

- Screening call with Recruiter

- Hiring Manager interview

- Technical interview (system design)

- Live coding

As part of our standard hiring process, we would like to inform you that a background check may be conducted at the final stage of recruitment through our third-party provider, Checkr.

description:
Health can’t wait . 

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

Disclaimer: We're open to hire Account Executives across our Paris, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes and Biarritz offices. 

⭐️ The Account Executive (mid-market) job

We’re expanding our Sales team in France and are looking for ‘full-stack’ Sales to engage with prospects and turn them into happy Alan customers. You will join a team that focuses on companies from one of the following segments: Tech & Engineering, Business Services & Media, Retail, Transport, HCR, Learn & Care, Food & Beverage or Metallurgy.

You will interact with everyone from HR executives to CEOs.

Meet Hakim in this article to learn more about makes the Metallurgy segment so interesting for an Account Executive. 

Why is our Vertical approach interesting? 

- Market potential: Vast and dynamic markets with significant structural challenges, offering fertile ground for a modern, tech-driven solution like Alan.

- Team readiness: We've honed our go-to-market strategy over the years, and it's paying off with increasing inbound leads and active field marketing driving strong pipeline momentum.

- Passionate teams: Our dedicated teams brings deep sector expertise and genuine passion for the clients we serve; every day in the field sharpens our edge and fuels our conviction.

- Growth opportunity: The addressable market is enormous, offering virtually unlimited opportunities for growth.

You’ll own the entire sales cycle, from prospecting to closing . The average sales cycle is 4-6 months , dealing with companies ranging from 30 to 300 employees, with an average ARR of 150K€ .

At Alan, Account Executives drive deals and close strategic opportunities with prospects . We sometimes handle some customer relationships to ensure the best possible onboarding. You’ll educate prospects, provide inspiring product demos, and onboard key stakeholders, making the transition from prospect to customer seamless.

We expect you to understand and apply the Alan Smart & Soft selling method . This method ensures the prospect experience is an integral part of the overall Alan customer experience—making it pleasant and delightful for everyone. We expect you to be instructive to prospects (Smart), as well as to define the best personalized high-touch strategy that suits best each prospect (Soft).

You’ll also help us grow and improve as a company , challenging us to enhance our product(s), methods, and strategy, and getting involved in initiatives to expand our customer base.

Meet Fanny Cibot who is Account Executive within the Business Services & Media Crew. 

⭐ Is it you we’re looking for?

You’ll be a great fit for the Metallurgy Team at Alan if you: 

- Have at least 4 years of experience managing the whole Sales cycle, from prospecting to closing. Prospection is a key part of the role;

- Have full working proficiency in French (C2 and above) and an advanced level in English .

- Are highly organized with exceptional follow-up skills ;

- Have empathy and are passionate about understanding and solving prospects' problems;

- Can influence through persuasion, negotiation, and consensus-building;

- Have a deep understanding of value drivers in recurring revenue business models;

- Have a great attitude and ability to collaborate in a small team;

- Are eager to learn fast and make an impact from day 1;

- Are based in (or willing to relocate to) Paris, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz. 

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range .

If you're still wondering whether this could be the best move for you, take a look at this article from Lucie Leflour, our Sales Lead in France. 

Everything else is a plus. We care about having a diversity of experiences, profiles and backgrounds in our team.

🙌 Perks & Benefits 

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need , and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Therefore, we offer: 

- Fair rewards . Generous equity packages complement your base salary, for permanent contracts only. 

- Flexible office with hybrid setup . Amazing office space at our Paris HQ or sponsored co-working hubs in Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

- All the tools you need . Top of the range equipment: Macbook Air, keyboard, laptop stand, monitor, and Bose noise-canceling headphones.

- Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours . Organize your time as you wish.

- Delightful healthcare insurance: Extremely comprehensive health insurance - 100% for you and your children, 90-100% for partners depending on your country (permanent contracts only). 

- Transport . Generous transit benefit

- Learning & Training opportunities . A highly flexible training policy free books and budget to attend and speak at conferences if the opportunity arises.

- Personal growth through coaching : At Alan, coaching isn't just a perk - it's core to who we are. Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture . 

- Parental leave . Extended parental leave for all new parents, for permanent contracts only. 

Important note: we hire people, not roles. 

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success.

description:
About EH Group Engineering 

EHG is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product is a significantly more compact fuel cell with high power density and lower costs of production. Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field. 

Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

Key Responsibilities: 

- Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

- Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

- Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

- Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

- Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

- Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

- Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

- Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

- Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

- Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

- Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

Skills and Experience Required: 

- BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

- Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

- Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

- Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

- Experience with functional safety (e.g. IEC 61508, ISO 13849), including SIL/PL determination and implementation of safety functions

- Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

- Experience with stationary and maritime power applications, with a focus on the US and EU markets and their respective standards and certification requirements

- Proven team player, with the ability to: 
(i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team 
(ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

- Solid knowledge of control theory, state machines and system identification

- Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

- Professional working language is in English.

Start date: Immediately

title: Responsable Qualité Multi-Sites - Piles à Combustible
description:
About EHG 

EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

The opportunity 

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

What you'll own 

- One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

- Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

- In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

- Supplier quality for a shared global supply base , working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

title: Robotics Integration Engineer
description:
About Enact 

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role You Will 

- Design, integrate and test the electromechanical systems at the core of our dexterous robots: actuator modules, joints, and end-effectors, sensors, PCBs, and cable harnesses into compact, reliable units for high-DoF robotics

- Bring hardware to life: lead system assembly & bring-up, debug across mechanics, electronics, and firmware, and work with controls & AI engineers to build a fully vertically integrated manipulation system

- Develop & build automated test setups to validate performance, durability, and reliability, and take systems from prototype to series production

What We're Looking For 

- Degree (BSc/MSc/PhD) in mechatronics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field

- 3+ years of work experience developing complex mechatronic systems that bridge mechanical design, electronics, and software

- Solid understanding of electric motors, encoders, sensors, and motor drivers, and how to integrate them into a working system

- Experience with system-level debugging and testing using tools such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, and data acquisition systems

- Comfortable with programming for test automation and data analysis (e.g., Python)

- Familiarity designing parts in CAD (e.g. Onshape)

- Hands-on experience with rapid prototyping, workshop tools, soldering, 3D printing, and prototype assembly/testing

- Fluency in English (spoken and written), with strong interpersonal and communication skills

Bonus Points If You Have 

- Hands-on development experience with high-DoF robotic systems (e.g., robotic arms, end-effectors, dexterous hands, or humanoids)

Most People roles ask you to run processes someone else built. This one asks you to build them, and to own one of them outright: how Eye rewards and recognises its people. This role has two halves, and you’ll split your time roughly evenly between them.

What you’ll do 

- Own Total Rewards end to end: run the annual salary review, keep our benchmarks honest, and build levelling and salary bands that make sense to managers and employees alike.

title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (Inference Stack Optimization)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and we run the models underneath it ourselves.

Kimchi Inference 

One API line and a customer's existing client just works: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron served serverless from our own GPU fleet (OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible, pay per token, spend visible per user, team, and key). When control matters, the same models run on the customer's own cluster instead. Behind that one line sits the machinery you'll own: SGLang and vLLM engines, B300 nodes, a shared cluster filesystem that holds every checkpoint exactly once, KV caches riding coding traffic with heavy prefix reuse, and the benchmark harness that gates every change we ship.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. Cold starts. Cost per token.

Move those four numbers in the right direction and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every loader you tune, every scheduler decision you land, every kernel you stare at shows up in a customer's p99 and on our P&L. Your mandate is the inference stack's optimization, whatever it takes, and the technical direction of how we optimize it is yours to argue with data.

The problem: the checkpoints run 0.3-1.5 TB, and the "right" serving configuration depends on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, and quantization tolerance, all variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a configuration once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. We don't: we took Kimi-K3 (1.5 TB) from over an hour cold-to-serving to under twelve minutes with a shared filesystem, O_DIRECT weight loaders, and node-local JIT caches, and we're nowhere near done. Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV caches are next.

Stack: Python; SGLang; vLLM; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; fastsafetensors; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; virtiofs shared filesystems; ClickHouse; OpenTelemetry; Prometheus; Grafana; GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've built real ML systems for 5+ years, and your portfolio shows depth in inference or training infrastructure, not just model training notebooks.

- Your Python is production-grade: services, not scripts.

- You've run vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM for real, and you have a working mental model of why an engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- You've measured quantization regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node setups hold no fear: tensor and expert parallelism, collective communication, and their practical failure modes.

- You know where the bytes live (page caches, O_DIRECT, network filesystems under terabyte-scale reads) and how fast they move.

- You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell a real win from a benchmark artifact.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with draft models, CUDA-graph capture, and scheduler tuning across the engine
fleet. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and inter-token latency separately; profile to find the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, storage, or
network) and fix it, not the one you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Hierarchical and paged attention, prefix caching on heavy-reuse coding traffic, eviction policies, quantized KV. A lot of the
unrealized throughput lives here, and you'll own it.

- Kill cold starts. Weight loaders (O_DIRECT, fastsafetensors-class), JIT and compile caches, shared-filesystem read paths. A 1.5 TB checkpoint has no business
taking an hour to reach serving.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8/INT4, FP8/FP4 across weights, activations, and KV, measured on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, prefill/decode disaggregation, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck
on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible
experiments.

title: Senior Applied ML Engineer | Kimchi (Model Router)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router 

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers' own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product's clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn't do the same work slower, it does less work. That's why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

- You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.

- You have real opinions about what LLM benchmarks measure, agentic harnesses included.

- You know enough serving reality (TTFT, decode speed, batching, prefix caching, concurrency) to model the objective honestly.

- You instrument before you optimize, error bars and all.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

title: Senior Product Manager - Search & Ranking
description:
At Catawiki, every day brings the extraordinary! Whether it’s Daniel Ricciardo’s Formula 1 Car , a Woolly Mammoth’s Skeleton , Lady Gaga's Jumpsuit or Usain Bolt’s running shoe , we encounter exceptional objects every day.

We’re a one-of-a-kind marketplace for buying and selling special objects. Each week, more than 100,000 unique items are auctioned, all carefully curated by our passionate in-house experts.

Having sold over 25 million unique objects, our mission is to become the world’s most popular destination for special objects. As a growing, diverse and sustainable scale-up, we proudly live by three core values. If these values resonate with you, we’d love to explore how you can join us.

- Taking ownership and driving impact 

- Being open to change and feedback

- Being passionate about our mission and our customers. 

Your mission 

Every Product Manager at Catawiki owns a meaningful part of the customer experience.

In Search and Ranking, your mission is to help buyers find the special objects they care about. You will shape how search, ranking and personalisation work across the buyer journey, making discovery more relevant and helping more buyers find objects they love.

This is a broad product area. It brings together buyer needs, expert curation, marketplace priorities, search experiences and machine learning. You will identify the most important opportunities, set a clear direction and lead a cross functional team from insight to measurable customer and business impact.

The solution is not prescribed. You may improve search relevance, ranking, recommendations or personalisation, or explore new AI enabled ways to help buyers discover objects. What matters is that you solve a meaningful customer problem, measure the impact and scale what works.

You will own the strategy, outcomes and execution for this area, working closely with Engineering, Design, Data Science, Marketing and Commercial teams.

What you will do 

- Set and communicate a clear product vision, strategy and roadmap for Search and Ranking.

- Own measurable outcomes across search relevance, discovery, engagement and buyer conversion.

- Use behavioural data, customer research and commercial insight to identify and prioritise the biggest opportunities.

- Turn ambiguous customer and business problems into clear hypotheses, prototypes and executable plans.

- Lead initiatives from early discovery through experimentation, launch and scaling.

- Define success metrics and build a rigorous experimentation agenda for search, ranking and personalisation.

- Work with machine learning engineers and data scientists to assess model quality, test new approaches and improve customer outcomes.

- Improve the relevance of search results and recommendations across the buyer journey.

- Integrate personalisation into the customer experience in ways that feel useful, coherent and trustworthy.

- Design, run and evaluate experiments, using positive, negative and inconclusive results to guide decisions.

- Use AI and rapid prototyping to test ideas early, reduce development risk and accelerate learning.

- Create clarity, momentum and accountability across teams, including when priorities or incentives differ.

- Communicate strategy, performance, tradeoffs and recommendations clearly to senior and C level stakeholders.

Who you are 

Three qualities matter most in this role.

Outcome ownership 

You take responsibility for customer and business results, not only for delivering features. You stay with the problem, remove obstacles and change direction when the evidence calls for it.

Systems thinking 

You understand how search, ranking, recommendations, auction dynamics, expert curation and marketplace health influence one another. You make thoughtful decisions across the full buyer journey.

Experimental rigour 

You use data, research, prototypes and controlled experiments to make decisions. You learn from negative results and can distinguish meaningful progress from activity.

You will also bring:

- At least five years of product management experience, preferably in consumer ecommerce, marketplaces or another digital product at scale.

- Experience owning a broad product area or customer journey, rather than only individual features.

- Experience defining product strategy or roadmaps for search, ranking, recommendations, personalisation or other machine learning products.

- Confidence working with product metrics, experiments and commercial performance.

- Experience designing, running and analysing A/B tests, including tests involving machine learning products.

- The ability to turn uncertain opportunities into clear hypotheses, prototypes and plans.

- A practical understanding of machine learning concepts and how models become useful product experiences.

- Experience working closely with machine learning engineers and data scientists to develop and improve customer facing features.

- Comfort using AI tools to prototype quickly and explore customer experiences.

- The ability to balance immediate commercial opportunities with longer term product and platform investments.

- Clear communication skills and the ability to influence senior leaders without relying on formal authority.

- The pace, resilience and judgement to maintain a high standard of execution in an ambiguous environment.

Where you will be 

This role is based in Amsterdam. We offer a relocation package for people currently living outside the Netherlands.

Why You'll Love Working with Us 

- Create a visible impact by working at scale in a global organisation serving millions of customers across 80+ categories. In our flat structure, every role has a broad scope and directly impacts both our customers and the business.

- Learn and grow through our Learning & Development initiatives, including clear development plans and mentorship programmes to support your career progression.

- A culture of connection defines us . We’re a passionate, diverse team of 800+ Catawikians representing 60+ nationalities. We foster an inclusive and queer-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to bring their full self to work.

Our Offices and Way of Working 

Our vibrant offices in Amsterdam and Lisbon are designed to inspire collaboration. Most Catawikians operate in a hybrid setup, combining office-based and remote work, with a minimum of two days per week in the office, unless a role is explicitly stated as fully remote or fully office-based.

Interested?

title: Manager Operations Planning & Performance
description:
Bij Crisp hebben we een missie: eten met meer smaak bereikbaar maken voor iedereen. Daarvoor moet elke schakel in onze operatie, van warehouse tot voordeur, dagelijks naadloos op elkaar aansluiten. Als Manager Operations Planning & Performance ben jij de spil tussen wat de klant bestelt en hoe wij dat logistiek waarmaken. Je brengt alle operationele schakels samen in één strakke, integrale planning en bouwt mee aan een betrouwbare operatie die klaar is om slim door te groeien.

Wat je gaat doen

Je bent eigenaar van de integrale operationele planning. Je vertaalt verwachte klantvraag naar concrete capaciteit op de weg (hoeveel bezorgers hebben we per dag en per hub nodig?) en bepaalt samen met de Operations Manager de planningsstrategie voor de korte en middellange termijn. Je zorgt voor een strakke planning tussen Delivery, Retentie en Warehouse. Zo werkt iedereen vanuit dezelfde basis en tilt jouw scherpe blik onze processen naar een hoger niveau.

- Je geeft leiding aan een team van routeplanners (werkstudenten en starters). Samen zorgen jullie dagelijks voor de meest efficiënte bezorgroutes. Jouw team staat in direct contact met de bezorghubs, het warehouse en de growth afdeling om de capaciteit af te stemmen

- Je werkt nauw samen met teams door de hele organisatie, van Tech en Analytics tot Recruitment. Om te weten wat er speelt, ben je regelmatig te vinden waar het gebeurt: op onze bezorghubs en in het warehouse.

- Je stuurt op operationele KPI’s (zoals Drops per Hour en Time per Stop ) en beheert belangrijke kostenlijnen. Samen met de Regiomanager en Business Analyst Delivery blijf je ons bezorgnetwerk continu optimaliseren.

- Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor de lijn tussen ons warehouse en de hubs. Je onderhoudt de contacten met vrachtwagenvervoerders, stuurt op prestaties ( On Time ) en kosten ( Cost per Drop ) en maximaliseert de vulgraad.

- Je kijkt altijd naar wat beter kan, houdt trends en innovaties in de markt in de gaten en draagt dit actief aan wanneer je hier kansen ziet. Je signaleert kansen in de operatie, maakt de impact inzichtelijk en leidt verbeterprojecten van idee tot implementatie, bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van servicetijd, automatisering van planningstaken of de inrichting van ons netwerk.

- Je bent onderdeel van het Delivery team en rapporteert aan de Head of Delivery.

Dit ben jij

- Je hebt HBO/WO werk- en denkniveau en minimaal 3 jaar werkervaring in operationele planning, logistiek of supply chain, bij voorkeur in een snelgroeiende e-commerce- of retailomgeving.

- Je beweegt je makkelijk door de hele organisatie, van de vloer tot het management. Je zoekt actief de samenwerking op en krijgt verschillende teams moeiteloos op één lijn. Je creëert draagvlak en krijgt mensen mee in een gezamenlijke aanpak, ook als je geen formele zeggenschap over ze hebt

- Je bent sterk met data. Je duikt zelf in de cijfers, bouwt een model of dashboard als dat nodig is, en vertaalt analyses naar concrete keuzes voor de operatie. Ervaring met SQL, BigQuery en Data Studio is een pré.

- Jij kijkt verder dan je eigen scope en overziet de hele keten. Je begrijpt hoe een keuze in de planning doorwerkt in het warehouse, op de weg en bij de klant, en je weet de juiste balans te vinden tussen kosten en kwaliteit.

- Je bent resultaatgericht en weet wat het is om eigenaarschap te nemen. Jij maakt dingen graag makkelijk en concreet. Complexe vraagstukken zet jij gemakkelijk om naar begrijpelijke acties.

- Je houdt het hoofd koel als het even spannend wordt. Pieken, onverwachte uitval of last-minute wijzigingen brengen je niet van je stuk; je prioriteert, plant opnieuw en zorgt dat de operatie doordraait.

- Je spreekt vloeiend Nederlands en Engels.

Wat wij bieden

- Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem.

- 27 vakantiedagen om bij te komen en op te laden.

title: Project Leider Bouw
description:
Monumental automatiseert de bouw met robotica en software. Onze missie is om de bouw software-defined en autonoom te maken – een toekomst waarin mooie gebouwen op maat in één dag verrijzen, met minimale inzet van handwerk.

We zijn een groeiend team van engineers, operators en technici, afkomstig van bedrijven als Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta en Google DeepMind. We staan nog aan het begin van het opbouwen van dit bedrijf, en dit is je kans om buitenproportioneel veel impact te maken op een probleem dat écht uitmaakt. Vanaf dag één werk je samen met een ervaren foundingteam, met een Series B van $32M achter ons onder leiding van Khosla Ventures en Plural.

Monumental zit in het centrum van Amsterdam, in een prachtig pand met een volledig uitgeruste werkplaats en een eigen testvloer voor robots. We bouwen de hele stack in-house – hardware én software. We zijn uitdrukkelijk geen hybride of remote-first bedrijf: robots en muren bouw je niet vanaf je keukentafel, dus we werken vijf dagen per week op locatie.

Lees meer over waarom wij vinden dat je je tijd aan de bouw zou moeten besteden, en over onze visie en ons bedrijf . Misschien vind je ons YouTube-kanaal interessant, de film van Based in Europe over hoe we het Europese woningtekort aanpakken , of deze video van Andreas Klinger over hoe ons kantoor eruitziet. 

Over de functie 

De afgelopen jaren is Monumental gegroeid van een werkend product en de eerste proefprojecten naar bouwen op grote schaal. Inmiddels hebben we een vloot van meer dan 150 robots, die metselwerk hebben uitgevoerd voor meer dan 90 woningen, een school, een buurthuis, een hotel en meer dan 150 meter kanaalwand.

Elke maand nemen we meer bouwprojecten aan, intern noemen we die ‘deployments’. We werken met meer robots en meer mensen en breiden vanuit Nederland uit naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk en de VS.

Als Hub Lead zet je onze eerste vestiging buiten het hoofdkantoor op, in het noorden van Nederland. Je begint met ons grootste bouwproject tot nu toe. Naarmate er meer projecten bijkomen, bouw je het team en de operatie verder uit. 

We zoeken mensen die breed inzetbaar zijn en een bouwproject willen leiden alsof het hun eigen bedrijf is. Achter elk project staat een Deployment Manager die van begin tot eind verantwoordelijk is. In de praktijk vervul je vijf rollen tegelijk: uitvoerder, operationeel manager, accountmanager, analist en projectmanager. Je maakt het bouwplan, voert het met je team als onderaannemer uit, onderhoudt het contact met de aannemer en zorgt dat we goed metselwerk op tijd opleveren. Dat doe je in de bouw, waar plannen voortdurend veranderen. Uiteindelijk leid je meerdere projecten tegelijk, waaronder complexe projecten waarbij veel op het spel staat.

De ene dag sta je bij zonsopgang op en ga je naar de bouwplaats. Je zaagt stenen, bewaakt de planning, stemt af met de hoofdaannemer en ziet je bouwplan steen voor steen werkelijkheid worden. De volgende dag zit je op onze vestiging, analyseer je de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en werk je aan systemen waarmee je bij het volgende project een betere marge haalt. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de oplevering en geeft knelpunten die je op de bouwplaats tegenkomt door aan ons R&D-team.

Dit is intensief, praktisch werk op locatie, waar je veel voldoening uit kunt halen. Robots gaan kapot, het weer slaat om en de aannemer verandert het plan. Jij zorgt dat de bouw doorgaat.

Je krijgt veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid. De rol past goed bij je als je eerder een bedrijf hebt opgericht, of als je een ondernemende functie zoekt waarin je veel invloed hebt op het resultaat.

Wat je gaat doen 

- De logistiek van een bouwproject plannen. Je bepaalt hoeveel en welke robots en mensen nodig zijn, stemt af met andere onderaannemers en maakt de dagelijkse planning. Tegelijk houd je het grotere geheel in het oog en begrijp je wat jouw keuzes betekenen voor de kosten en opbrengsten per project.

- Op de bouwplaats het team aansturen, begeleiden en motiveren. Je onderhoudt het contact met hoofdaannemers en andere betrokkenen, vertegenwoordigt Monumental en legt uit wat we doen. Je schakelt net zo makkelijk met steigerbouwers als met de CEO’s van de grootste hoofdaannemers en onze engineers.

- Operationele systemen opzetten waarmee elk project beter verloopt dan het vorige. Je ziet waar tijd en middelen verloren gaan, past processen aan en verbetert de marge.

- Samenwerken met bestaande klanten en zorgen dat daar nieuwe bouwprojecten uit voortkomen. In de toekomst doe je dat ook voor aanverwante productlijnen buiten het metselwerk.

- Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en voorstellen doen om de kosten en opbrengsten per project steeds verder te verbeteren.

- Helpen bij het werven en interviewen van nieuwe robotoperators en deployment operators.

Wat we zoeken 

- Minimaal drie jaar ervaring startupervaring, als operator, manager, of founder.

- Nederlands als moedertaal. De bouwsector is sterk lokaal georganiseerd, dus dit is een vereiste voor de functie.

- Je communiceert helder en makkelijk met mensen met uiteenlopende achtergronden.

- Je bent bereid om letterlijk je handen vuil te maken om het werk gedaan te krijgen.

- Je komt snel in actie, zet door en krijgt dingen voor elkaar. In deze functie draait het vooral om uitvoeren.

- Je kunt goed omgaan met hoge werkdruk. Op bouwplaatsen gaat regelmatig iets mis en staat er veel op het spel. Daar komt bij dat we nieuwe technologie inzetten waarvan we nog niet alle mogelijke storingen kennen.

- Je denkt scherp en leert graag. Welke achtergrond je ook hebt, je zult in deze rol veel en snel moeten leren. Het werk kan elke drie tot zes maanden als een nieuwe baan voelen. Je leert veel over de bouw, robotica en werken in een snelgroeiend technologiebedrijf.

- Je hebt ervaring met het aansturen van een klein team en weet hoe je mensen begeleidt en motiveert.

- Je bent operationeel en analytisch sterk. Je kunt een helder operationeel plan uitwerken in een spreadsheet, een winst- en verliesrekening presenteren en verschillende scenario’s doorrekenen, inclusief de factoren die het resultaat bepalen. Je bent een sterke projectmanager.

Waarom Monumental? 

Bij Monumental werken betekent vooroplopen in een beweging die de bouwsector wezenlijk wil veranderen. Jouw werk heeft hier niet alleen impact op het bedrijf, maar op de toekomst van hoe we bouwen. Als je gedreven wordt door innovatie, graag complexe uitdagingen aanpakt en klaar bent om echt verschil te maken, horen we graag van je.

Voor open sollicitaties (als je geen rol ziet die precies past) kun je ons mailen op: 

Helaas bieden we op dit moment geen stageplekken aan.

Voldoe je niet aan alle eisen hierboven, maar ben je enthousiast over Monumental en denk je dat je ons toch kunt helpen moeilijke problemen op te lossen? Neem dan contact op. We verwelkomen generalisten die op resultaat gericht zijn en graag on the job leren.

title: Director, Expanded Access Program Operations
description:
About myTomorrows 

myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options. 

We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem. 

We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. Our services include clinical trial patient recruitment, Expanded Access Program management and Real-World Data collection. 

With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. In October 2025, we closed a €25M investment with Avego Healthcare Capital to fuel our global ambitions and scale the business. 

Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today.

You’ll be a core member of the Operations Leadership Team and report directly to our COO (Vanessa says hi). This role is perfect for someone who thrives on complexity, builds high‑performing teams, and raises the operational bar—while balancing patient‑first decision‑making with a strong commercial mindset.

Geographic Requirement: This role is open to candidates in The Netherlands, United Kingdom, Canada and USA. For candidates in North America , to ensure seamless collaboration with our teams, applicants must reside within the EST or CST time zones .

What you'll do in this role: 

- Own the end-to-end operating model for EAP Program + Site Management, ensuring scalable and compliant delivery

- Translate strategy and portfolio forecasts into capacity planning, org design and hiring priorities

- Build resilient coverage and escalation models across the portfolio (no single points of failure)

- Lead the EAP Program Management team to deliver consistent execution across clients and geographies

- Lead the EAP Site Management team to ensure strong site engagement, workload balance and service performance

- Drive standardisation and continuous improvement across ways of working, tooling and operational excellence

- Set and run a strong governance rhythm: KPIs, performance reviews, risk management and quality oversight

- Grow a bar-raising leadership bench through coaching, performance management and succession planning

- Partner with Finance, People and Operations on budgeting, workforce planning and scale-up decisions

What you bring to the table: 

- You have 8–10+ years experience leading and managing expanded access programs.

- Experience in a market access setting and with multi-country reimbursement strategies is a plus.

- You understand the EAP business, and have a strong and proven commercial and client service mindset.

- You have proven experience building and leading high performance teams.

- You know how to lead managers and scale operational teams in complex settings

- You have an exceptionally strong understanding of compliance, regulatory frameworks and operational requirements in the context of Expanded Access Programs

- You have a track record of operational excellence: scaling delivery, managing risk, and raising performance standards

- You are a strategic thinker with strong execution focus — you simplify complexity and drive outcomes

- You are a confident stakeholder manager who can align senior leaders and external partners

- You hold a high bar for quality and accountability, with calm leadership under pressure

What success in the first 6 months looks like: 

- Have full grip on the EAP portfolio and delivery realities — and you can clearly articulate the biggest operational opportunities and risks (and have recommendations on how to address them)

- Create clarity across Program & Site Management: ownership, workflows, escalation paths, and what “great” looks like

- Are seen as a trusted Operations Leadership Team member who raises the bar and builds momentum.

Equal opportunities 

myTomorrows is an Equal Opportunity Employer and, beyond upholding discrimination-free practices, we are committed to cultivating a workplace where difference and diversity are protected and celebrated. title: Team Lead, Data Engineering
description:
We are looking for a Data Engineering Team Lead to lead the Data Platform team at DataSnipper.

Every decision DataSnipper makes about its products runs through the data platform: which features land, which customers are getting value, what we bill for, what we fix next, and which AI capabilities add the most value. You will lead a team of two data engineers who own the systems that make that possible. That means how usage events get captured across a growing set of products, how they become trustworthy models in Snowflake, and how Customer Success, Product and GTM get to answers without waiting on us.

This is a player-coach role in a small, high-ownership team . You are responsible for the people, the roadmap and the technical direction, and you stay hands-on enough to ship alongside the team and make architectural calls credibly. At DataSnipper, Team Lead is our entry point into engineering management: the same people, delivery and product responsibilities as an Engineering Manager, on a smaller team.

We are a handful of people serving the whole company, so your judgment about what not to build matters as much as what the team ships.

About DataSnipper

DataSnipper is the driving force behind an intelligent automation platform that’s transforming the world of audit and finance.

Founded in 2017, DataSnipper has skyrocketed and is now OFFICIALLY the fastest-growing software company in the Netherlands according to Deloitte Fast50 and recently achieved Unicorn status in our latest funding round. With over 400.000 users in 125+ countries and a second base in the heart of New York City, DataSnipper is shaking things up. And we’re not stopping there. At DataSnipper, we’re always on the lookout for innovators who think outside of the box. New ideas aren’t just welcomed at DataSnipper–they’re essential.

What your team owns

The Data Platform team works across three areas:

- Data Platform : reliable, scalable infrastructure that gets the right data to the right place

- Internal Analytics : a self-service platform so every team can be data-informed without a ticket

- Customer-facing Analytics : the dashboards and exports customers use to see the value they get from DataSnipper

Concretely, you would be walking into billions of usage events flowing from our Excel Add-in, web apps and product backends through Azure Event Hubs into Snowflake ; a dbt estate built on medallion principles and managed in dbt Cloud ; Terraform-managed Snowflake and Azure infrastructure; and a set of product teams shipping AI agents faster than we can instrument them .

You will also find real, named open problems rather than a tidy platform: event capture mid-consolidation, multiple methods of user attribution, and a data quality layer that is designed but not yet built. We would rather tell you that up front.

What you will do

Lead the team

- Lead a team of two data engineers through outcomes, not tasks : set clear goals with the team and trust them to figure out how

- Make the team measurably better: raise the engineering bar, grow each engineer into bigger problems, and address performance issues directly when they arise

- Run regular 1:1s, give clear and timely feedback, and own each engineer's goals and development

- Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, documentation and operational excellence

- Take part in hiring and help shape the team's scope as it evolves

Own direction and delivery

- Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success and GTM to shape the team's roadmap , turning vague data requests into scoped, well-defined work

- Make the trade-offs a small team serving the whole company needs: what to build, what to defer, and when a request shouldn't become a pipeline

- Set the technical direction and make the architectural calls that shape the team's systems

- Keep Snowflake performance and cost , tech debt, dependencies and compliance obligations (audit logging, vulnerability remediation, Vanta evidence) visible and under control

- Be the person other engineering teams come to when they need to instrument something new

Stay hands-on in the data platform

- Contribute to the event ingestion architecture end to end: Azure Event Hubs, Snowpipe, Fivetran, and our shared Python/TypeScript event client libraries

- Build and review dbt transformation pipelines that stay reliable as volume, source count and model complexity grow

- Define and enforce event contracts and schemas so product teams can instrument new features without silent breakage downstream

- Evolve the core data models (event, user, license, company) and integrate new sources such as product backends, MongoDB, HubSpot and billing

- Guide reverse ETL and activation work that pushes modeled data back into HubSpot, MongoDB, Postgres and GTM reporting

What you bring

Leadership

- At least 1 year leading engineers as a team lead or engineering manager: 1:1s, feedback, goal setting, performance, and development

- An empowerment style of leadership : you lead through outcomes and trust, not by assigning tasks

- Early evidence of growing engineers and raising a team's bar, and the willingness to address performance issues directly

- Strong product aptitude : you can challenge the framing of a request, translate stakeholder needs into technical solutions, and make roadmap trade-offs

Data engineering

- 7+ years in data engineering or a closely related backend/platform role, with a track record of owning a data platform area end to end

- Deep SQL and strong Python , including query optimization and performance tuning on a cloud warehouse

- Production experience with a cloud data warehouse (we use Snowflake ) and a modern transformation framework (we use dbt )

- Experience with event-driven / streaming ingestion and its failure modes: schema drift, duplication, late data, backfills

- Experience on a cloud platform at the infrastructure level (we're on Azure ; AWS/GCP transfers fine)

- Solid data modeling fundamentals and the ability to defend a modeling decision to both engineers and business stakeholders

- Experience operating data systems in production with a focus on reliability, observability and maintainability

How you work

- Excellent communication in English and genuine comfort working directly with non-technical stakeholders

- Bias to action, a strong sense of ownership, and the judgment to prioritize when demand exceeds capacity

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in a startup or scale-up , ideally as an early member of a data team

- Experience hiring engineers or helping a team expand its scope

- Experience with product analytics tooling (Mixpanel, RudderStack) and warehouse-native BI (Netspring/Optimizely Analytics, Omni, Embeddable, or similar)

- Experience building data products for AI or agent consumption : semantic layers, metrics layers, MCP servers, or governed self-service access

- Experience with Terraform , Docker and data governance at scale

- Reverse ETL experience and familiarity with CRM data models (HubSpot, Salesforce) or customer success platforms

description:

We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. 

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. 

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. 

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. 

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

This is a structured 18–24 month global programme designed to launch high-potential commercial careers. You don’t need prior sales or payments experience; what you need is ambition, curiosity, resilience, and the drive to build relationships and solve complex problems.

Throughout the programme, you will master enterprise sales: researching strategic accounts, engaging senior decision-makers, conducting sharp discovery conversations, and building pipeline that drives real business growth.

High performers transition into Sales, Account Management, and other commercial roles across the business. Many of our top commercial leaders, including our Chief Revenue Officer, started their journey at Checkout.com as BDRs or interns. Whether you are a recent graduate, an early-career professional with 1–3 years of experience, or a career switcher, what matters most is your hunger to learn and achieve.
